info.title: Ticketing Platform API
info.description:
High-concurrency ticketing platform API.

**Authentication** — Call `POST /api/v1/auth/login` from an allowed Origin or Referer. Registration
also requires this. The browser sends the HttpOnly session cookie automatically on same-origin
requests. Call `GET /api/v1/auth/me` to obtain the session's `csrf_token`, then enter that token
as `X-CSRF-Token` when authorizing Swagger UI. Try a write such as `POST /api/v1/auth/logout`.
The payment provider callback authenticates separately using the signed `Mockpay-Signature` header.

**Errors** — API problems use `application/problem+json` (RFC 9457) with a stable `code`, a
`retryable` flag and the `request_id` to quote when reporting problems. The readiness probe
reports dependency checks in its own diagnostic response.

get.description: Public probe for process liveness. A read has no side effects.
Public probe for database, Redis and schema readiness. Each read checks current state.

503.description: One or more readiness checks failed.

post.description: A caller from an allowed origin can create a User account. The email is unique. Repeating a successful registration returns a conflict. Requests are rate-limited.

post.summary: Sign in and set the session cookie
post.description: A caller from an allowed origin can sign in with an active account. Each successful request creates a session and returns a CSRF token. Requests are rate-limited.
Revoke the current authenticated session. Revocation takes effect on the next request. Repeating the request with the revoked cookie returns 401.

get.summary: Get the current user and CSRF token
get.description: Read the authenticated user's current account and CSRF token.
Admins can list accounts in ascending ID order. Each page uses the last ID as its cursor, so inserts do not shift accounts already returned.

get.description: All roles can read published events. Drafts are visible to the owner and administrators. The idempotent read returns event fields and zones from one snapshot with a strong ETag.

patch.description: Only the owner or an administrator may edit. If-Match guards concurrent edits and advances the ETag on success. Sales dates and zones are frozen after publication. A draft zone replacement retains seats in zones with the same code.

delete.description: The owner or an administrator can delete an event with no orders. The event lock serializes deletion with other event writes. A repeat after successful deletion returns 404.

post.description: The owner or an administrator may publish with the current If-Match once seats exist and no import is active. The event lock serializes publication with import admission. Repeating with the current ETag after publication returns the same version.

get.description: All roles may read published event zones. Only the owner and administrators may read draft zones. An idempotent read returns counts from one database snapshot.

get.description: Only the parent event owner or an administrator may download row errors. This idempotent read returns the current attempt's committed errors in physical line order. Formula- leading text is escaped.

Administrators and viewers may export any event. Users may export only their own. Viewer reports pseudonymize buyers per event. The idempotent read generates a new workbook from one database snapshot. A concurrent export returns 429.

post.description: Users and admins can reserve 1 to 4 seats for a published event during its sales window. Specific seats are locked without waiting. Zone allocation skips seats locked by other transactions. Quota and all seats are reserved atomically. Reuse the Idempotency-Key with the same request within 24 hours to replay the original response with Idempotent-Replayed: true. An in-flight request returns 409 and Retry-After: 1. After it completes, changing the operation, resource or body returns 422.

post.summary: Cancel an order or request its refund
post.description: Owners and admins can cancel a pending order and release its seats immediately, or request a refund for a paid order. Paid seats remain reserved until the refund is confirmed. Cancellation, expiry and payment decisions serialize on the order. Reuse the Idempotency-Key with the same request within 24 hours to replay the original response with Idempotent-Replayed: true. An in-flight request returns 409 and Retry-After: 1. After it completes, changing the operation, resource or body returns 422.

post.summary: Start or resume checkout for an order
post.description: The owner may request checkout while the hold is active. Concurrent keys use the same chargeable attempt. Retry the same request with the same Idempotency-Key within 24 hours to resume that attempt and receive its current result with Idempotent-Replayed: true. An active checkout returns 201. Replaying the same key after the order was paid returns 200, and after a terminal attempt returns 402. A new key for an order that is no longer awaiting payment returns 409 order-not-payable. A declined payment can be retried with a new key while the hold remains active. Advisory-lock contention returns 409 with Retry-After: 1. A committed key reused for another request returns 422.

get.description:
Any authenticated role may read a published event. Drafts are visible to User-role owners and administrators. Missing and hidden events return 404.

Read-only and safe to retry. Layout, seat state and the assigned stream sequence come from one repeatable-read database snapshot. Concurrent requests on the same API process share a refresh. A cached result is at most one second old and is bypassed when its layout version is below `min_layout_ver`. The response carries the database version even if it is below the requested minimum. Resume the stream using `last_seq`.

get.summary: Subscribe to a resumable seat update stream
get.description:
Any authenticated role may read a published event. Drafts are visible to User-role owners and administrators. Missing and hidden events return 404.

The read-only SSE stream accepts the last **applied** sequence in `Last-Event-ID`. Start with a snapshot and send its `last_seq`. Omitting the header tails the live head. Registration captures a live head and replays through it before following new frames. Delivery resumes at the next sequence and uses PostgreSQL when a ring frame is missing or overlaps the cursor. Apply only newer seat versions. At process capacity, new event IDs receive a retryable `503 server-busy`.

- `delta`, with `id: <to>` and payload `{"from": 10, "to": 12, "changes": [[0, "held", 2]], "ts": "2026-11-21T00:00:00Z"}`. The inclusive range covers all coalesced outbox rows and `ts` is their earliest outbox creation time. If `from > last_applied + 1`, reconnect from the last applied sequence.
- `layout`, with `id: <seq>`: `{"layout_ver": 3}`. Fetch a snapshot with `min_layout_ver=3` before applying deltas. Resume at that snapshot's sequence.
- `progress`, every second: `{"head": 12, "oldest_unassigned_age_ms": 0}`. If progress advances beyond the applied cursor for more than three seconds or the oldest unassigned change exceeds two seconds, show the state as stale.
- `resync`, followed by EOF: `{"reason": "replay-unavailable"}`. This includes missing replay rows and replay capacity exhaustion. Fetch a new snapshot and reconnect. A stalled socket may close before the frame arrives.
- A heartbeat comment is sent every 15 seconds. Revoked sessions are disconnected. Bytes already handed to the transport can still arrive.

parameters.name: last-event-id

schema.description: Last applied sequence, or last_seq from a new snapshot
schema.title: Last-Event-Id

get.description: Admins can read a UTC interval with an inclusive start and exclusive end, up to one hour per call. Each read is a snapshot. Late edge logs may revise recent samples.

Admins receive the latest completed second with edge, app and per-event business metrics. Each frame is a consistent database snapshot. Reconnecting resumes at the latest second. The stream checks the session every second.

200.description: SSE frames with event metrics and a JSON data object.

get.description: Admins can read a page of alerts by state. Reads are repeatable for the same database state. Use before_id to page through older occurrences while new alerts arrive.

Admins receive the latest active and recently resolved alert occurrences, up to 250. The stream reads durable state each second and works across replicas and Redis outages. A reconnect starts with the current snapshot. The session is checked every second.

200.description: SSE frames with event alerts and a JSON data object.

post.description: Admins with a valid CSRF token can acknowledge an alert. Concurrent or repeated acknowledgements return the first admin and timestamp. Acknowledgement records receipt.
